title: Telefónica and IQM to Deploy Community of Madrid's First On-Premises Quantum Computer at Universidad Politécnica de Madrid
excerpt: Telefónica and IQM Quantum Computers are deploying the first quantum computer in the Community of Madrid, an IQM Spark system at Universidad Politécnica de Madrid (UPM) by late 2026. This is their third quantum processor in Spain, aiming to provide local access to quantum hardware for research and education. Telefónica is also expanding its quantum technology portfolio, including QKD networks and post-quantum cryptography.
content:
European telecommunications operator Telefónica and superconducting quantum hardware provider IQM Quantum Computers have partnered to deploy the first quantum computer in the Community of Madrid. Under the initiative, an on-premises IQM Spark quantum processing system will be installed at the Universidad Politécnica de Madrid (UPM) before the end of 2026.

The system marks the third IQM quantum processor deployed in Spain via Telefónica, expanding upon the two systems previously delivered to the Galician Supercomputing Centre (CESGA). Designed for education, academic research, and algorithm benchmarking, the Madrid deployment provides regional universities, hospitals, research institutions, and technology startups with direct, local access to physical quantum hardware.

Expanding On-Premises QPU Infrastructure and Post-Quantum Security

The on-premises deployment model provides local researchers with full infrastructure control, eliminating latency and data sovereignty constraints associated with third-party remote cloud environments. The UPM facility will serve as a central research hub for exploring quantum algorithms in material science, biomedical modeling, and logistics optimization.

Alongside the hardware installation, Telefónica is expanding its quantum technology portfolio across Spain, including the deployment of Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) networks and post-quantum cryptography (PQC) standards to secure inter-data-center communications across healthcare, defense, and public administration sectors.
